hero.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting on Southeast Rivergreen Circle in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots.

When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Judlin Stokes, 22.

Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved. Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public.

All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police. The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Spain Defeats Argentina 1-0 to Win 2026 World Cup in Extra Time
cards.body:
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship in a match that remained scoreless through regulation time. Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute of extra time, pouncing on a bouncing ball in the box during the opening moment of the second 15-minute period. He used his left foot to bury a shot just under the crossbar and into the back of the net. The victory marks Spain's second World Cup championship and first since 2010.

Spain dominated possession and shot attempts throughout the match. The team took 15 shots in regulation compared to Argentina's zero and had nine corners to Argentina's one. Despite this overwhelming dominance, Lionel Messi and Argentina managed to hang on and force extra time. Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez made 10 saves during the afternoon, the most ever in a World Cup final. His crucial saves kept Argentina in the match despite Spain's relentless attack.

The match turned in Spain's favor when Argentina's Enzo Fernandez received his second yellow card in second-half stoppage time, forcing Argentina to finish with only 10 players. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, and the referee immediately pulled out the card. About two minutes after play resumed, another foul gave Lamine Yamal a chance to win it from about 22 yards out on a free kick. Yamal's strike was curling toward the right post when Martinez dived to knock it away for his 10th save. He leaped to his feet, punching the air and imploring the crowd to get loud before the whistle sent the game to extra time.

With its victory, Spain became the first nation to simultaneously hold the World Cup crowns in both men's and women's soccer. The match was the 104th and last of the biggest World Cup ever, a 48-team event that played out over the United States, Canada and Mexico. Because there were more matches than any previous World Cup, it was no surprise that there were more goals than all other editions. The tournament produced 308 goals in total. According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup was officially the most attended ever.

cards.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
cards.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
cards.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters, suspends 2 others after hazing investigation
cards.teaser: An independent investigation found senior firefighters used a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024. The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally.

Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County workplace culture assessment found intense peer pressure at Station 1A
cards.teaser: A 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing.
cards.body:
Attorney Susan Gainey conducted a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment that found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training.

The St. Lucie County Fire District released investigative reports on Saturday detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. Administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty during shifts in March and September 2024.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr Breaks Mile World Record in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 Saturday at a Diamond League event in London, breaking a 27-year-old world record.
cards.body:
Josh Kerr of Great Britain ran the mile in 3:42.66 Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999. The 27-year-old record fell at a Diamond League event where Kerr made no secret he was targeting the long-standing mark. Earlier in the week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor Brooks dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. The shoe company said Friday that "this is the moment Josh Kerr stands to make history and bring the mile record home."

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles and set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. American Yared Nuguse finished second in the race in 3:45.69. The record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.

According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program emphasizes that pool alarms are not a standalone safety solution but rather part of a comprehensive approach to water safety.

The program offers one alarm per household to Martin County residents who have a residential pool. There are no income or priority group requirements for the program, making it available to any qualifying resident regardless of financial status. The alarms are available while supplies last, so residents interested in obtaining one should act promptly. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well, noting that Boston is seeing great demand. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast residents avoid lettuce amid E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks
cards.teaser: Families across the Treasure Coast are changing their diets to avoid contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks, with five confirmed local cases since May.
cards.body:
Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected by contaminated produce, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations.

At restaurants, grocery stores and fast-food chains, some families say they are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. In Boynton Beach, Hendriette Peckens said she bought oranges, bread and apples instead of produce and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner. In downtown West Palm Beach, George Lorenz said he is taking precautions while grabbing lunch with his father on Clematis Street.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers. She recommends foods like bananas, melons and avocados, and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. She recommends avoiding bagged lettuce if possible and instead buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball Restricts iPad Use to Prevent AI Decision Making
cards.teaser: MLB made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night to prevent artificial intelligence from helping make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. In many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches, according to MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Instituting the prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments, Sword wrote. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Security Ramped Up for World Cup Final at New Jersey Stadium
cards.teaser: The World Cup final Sunday received a Level 1 Special Event designation, the highest possible security classification, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal Face Off in World Cup Final 19 Years After Photo Shoot
cards.teaser: A 2007 photo shoot captured teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal for a UNICEF charity calendar. The two now meet in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing baby boy Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Luck dictated that Yamal's mother, who appears in the calendar photo, won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later. The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.

Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the AP, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but now, with the World Cup final looming, Monfort said interest in his photos has skyrocketed. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets, while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. The 58-year-old photographer is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program, led by Summer Faerman, connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds, David Jolly Lead Florida Governor's Race as Primary Nears
hero.teaser: Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey rele
hero.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republicans, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8%, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and received President Donald Trump's endorsement.

The Republican primary has grown increasingly contentious as Collins, who was appointed lieutenant governor by Gov. Ron DeSantis in August 2025, attempts to consolidate support despite not receiving DeSantis's endorsement. During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, saying the primary is between Donalds and himself. Meanwhile, Fishback faces challenges on multiple fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments.

Collins is also challenging whether Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing on the residency question is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. The residency challenge adds another complication to Fishback's campaign as he attempts to gain traction in a race where Donalds maintains a significant polling advantage over the rest of the Republican field.

On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities, with the alleged scheme operating from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, and Govoni served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. The connection nonetheless presents a challenge for Jolly as he seeks to maintain his lead in the Democratic primary while managing questions about his past associations with individuals now facing serious federal charges.

hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service, which warns that conditions fueling these fires will persist throughout the summer months.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said this is peak season for brush fires in the region. The summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them highly receptive when lightning strikes occur. However, Grubitch emphasized that residents should not be alarmed by these conditions, as they are typical for this time of year. He explained that while rain often extinguishes fires immediately after they start, some fires can travel underground and resurface days later, making them more difficult to detect and contain.

The Florida Forest Service is relying on public assistance to help monitor and respond to brush fires quickly. Grubitch stressed that residents play a crucial role in helping the department do its job effectively. He urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot, emphasizing the importance of immediate notification. According to Grubitch, if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control.

With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

hero.teaser: An independent investigation found senior firefighters used a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024. The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally.

Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process.

cards.headline: Unity in the Community event connects Fort Pierce families with services and public safety demonstrations
cards.teaser: The annual Fort Pierce event brought together families with community resources and public safety demonstrations.
cards.body: The Unity in the Community event in Fort Pierce connected families with services, public safety demonstrations and community resources. The annual event builds bridges between police and residents in the city.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County workplace culture assessment found intense peer pressure at Station 1A
cards.teaser: A 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing.
cards.body:
Attorney Susan Gainey conducted a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment that found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training.
